prints.title: Ghost headphones
prints.description: The lite design: charcoal, gray, and ivory PLA headphones with a 71 mm cushion gap, sized for a 76 mm oatmeal gauze ghost. They were printed on 17 Oct 2026 (26 min and 13 g). Show in setting puts them on a display figure of that ghost, holding a pumpkin (the figure wasn't printed).
prints.material: PLA Matte, charcoal, gray, and ivory
prints.alt: Small charcoal headphones with gray cushions and ivory rings

iterations.label: v1
iterations.note: The original full design, also sized for a 76 × 63.5 × 76 mm head with a 71 mm cushion gap. The top band pad is a separate gray part. It was not printed. The lite design — same fit, with the band and pad in charcoal — is the one that was printed on 17 Oct 2026 and is shown on the ghost.

photo.alt: Render of the original full headphone design, with a gray pad on the band

iterations.label: v2
iterations.note: A smaller revision for a 63 × 53 × 63 mm head with a 58 mm cushion gap. It does not fit the 76 mm gauze ghost, and it is not the design on the figure.

photo.alt: Render of the smaller v2 headphones, sized for a 63 mm head

prints.title: Sink caddy
prints.description: A two-part organizer custom-fit to the sink: a draining tray and a removable holder for brushes, a sponge, and a soap ring. The tray was printed on 23 Oct 2026 and the organizer on 27 Oct, both in charcoal matte PLA.
prints.alt: A charcoal two-part sink caddy, with a low draining tray and a removable deck of cups, a sponge well, and a perforated ring dish

iterations.label: orig
iterations.note: Noah's Tinkercad original, saved as three STLs: an 83 mm-tall organizer-like body whose footprint (~168 × 198 mm) is in the same coordinates later versions use, a ~20 mm-tall part, and a thin ~3 mm part.

photo.alt: Render of the original Tinkercad sink caddy body

iterations.label: v2
iterations.note: First Python redesign as a two-part tray plus organizer. The deck has 9 drain slots and six posts; the sponge well is 125 × 32 mm. Sliced, but not recorded as printed.

photo.alt: Render of sink caddy v2, tray and organizer

iterations.label: v3
iterations.note: Same overall footprint. Drain slots reduced from 9 to 5, and the cup, ring, and sponge layout was rearranged (the ring-to-sponge wall gap in the stats went to 0 mm). A sponge-section render appears from this version on.

iterations.label: v4
iterations.note: The outline was extended toward the faucet (footprint +Y 20 mm to 71.5 mm). The small cup moved behind, and the sponge well was rotated to sit parallel to the sink edge (inner 125 × 30 mm). Ten drain slots.

photo.alt: Render of sink caddy v4, extended toward the faucet

iterations.label: v4.1
iterations.note: Fit was checked against a photo of the existing caddy on the actual sink. The faucet-end outline was pulled back (+Y 71.5 mm to 61.8 mm) for 31.5 mm of faucet clearance, and the sponge well was shortened to 115 × 30 mm.

iterations.label: v4.2
iterations.note: Holder positions match v4.1. Deck drain slots were dropped (0 in the stats). A print-orientation study (printB) was added; still not recorded as printed.

iterations.label: v4.3
iterations.note: From v4.2B: no posts, a 4 mm deck, a sink-side drain wall (arcade) up to the deck, and a straight faucet end. A skirt was added (2.4 mm thick, 8 mm below the counter, 0.5 mm edge gap). Volumes increased (tray 226.6 cm³, organizer 186.2 cm³).

photo.alt: Render of sink caddy v4.3, with skirt and arcade drain wall

iterations.label: v4.4
iterations.note: A 3 mm lip (1.6 mm thick, 0.4 mm clearance, 447 mm long) was added, with a 40 mm skirt taper. The tray mesh became watertight; tray volume went from 226.6 cm³ to 212.6 cm³.

photo.alt: Render of sink caddy v4.4, with a lip along the tray

iterations.label: v4.5
iterations.note: The locating lip was extended from 447 mm to 493 mm, running continuously around the tray except at the open sink curve. The faucet-end deck was trimmed 2 mm (plus 0.17 mm for a chamfer gap), and the sponge well was shifted 2.2 mm along its axis to keep its fillet margin. Tray volume went from 212.6 cm³ to 215.7 cm³; the organizer went from 185.4 cm³ to 184.8 cm³.

photo.alt: Render of sink caddy v4.5, the printed tray and organizer

prints.title: Glasses rack
prints.description: A one-piece holder that hooks over a nightstand drawer wall so three pairs of glasses stand upright like pencils in a cup, while the drawer still shuts. Printed in charcoal matte PLA, standing on end, with no supports.
prints.alt: A charcoal one-piece rack with three backward-leaning sleeves and a hook that fits over a drawer wall

iterations.label: v1
iterations.note: A modular three-piece concept. It was superseded because a shallower lean did not keep the tallest pair under the 155 mm drawer opening.

photo.alt: Render of the earlier modular glasses rack

prints.title: Minecraft figures
prints.description: Three matching 38.4 mm desk cubes: a creeper, a jack-o'-lantern, and a skeleton, each with its game texture built as relief in four colors. They line up 15 mm apart. The creeper slices at 7 h 20 min and the skeleton at 8 h 2 min; the jack-o'-lantern's time wasn't recorded.
prints.material: PLA, Bambu Green, Mistletoe Green, Ivory White, Charcoal, Mandarin Orange, Cocoa Brown, Desert Tan, Bone White, and Nardo Gray
prints.alt: Three small textured cubes in a row: a green creeper face, an orange jack-o'-lantern, and a bone-white skeleton face

prints.title: Jungle Boyz
prints.description: A four-color desk nameplate for Collin's Minecraft YouTube channel: JUNGLE BOYZ lettering, jungle trees and vines, and an ocelot, standing in a row of grass blocks. The plaque's tab drops into the stand and leans back 6°.
prints.material: PLA, black, brown, green, and tan
prints.alt: A four-color pixel-art nameplate reading JUNGLE BOYZ, with trees, vines, and an ocelot, standing on a grass-block base

prints.title: Watching movies
prints.description: A 248 × 158 × 20 mm tray with a four-color inlaid illustration in red, gold, black, and cream, built from a photograph. It's designed for the X2D AMS, and I recommend 0.16 mm layers on the inlay.
prints.material: PLA, black, red, gold, and cream
prints.alt: A black rectangular tray with a four-color inlaid picture in red, gold, black, and cream

prints.title: Fluke mount
prints.description: A holster that clips onto the folded front lip of a lab-bench shelf and holds a Fluke 115 multimeter below and in front of the shelf, tipped slightly forward.
prints.alt: A charcoal holster with an open-fronted pocket and a wedge-shaped clip behind it

photos.alt: A green 3D-printed mount clipped to the front lip of a lab bench shelf, holding a yellow Fluke 115 multimeter

prints.title: Shower caddy stopper
prints.description: A snap-on sleeve that covers the shower arm from its bend down to the shower head. The wire caddy's hanger hooks over the arm next to the wall flange, and the stopper keeps it from sliding down toward the head.
prints.alt: A charcoal half-pipe sleeve angled downward, with a flared end bent level at the top

photos.alt: A white 3D-printed stopper on a shower arm between the wall flange and the shower head, holding a wire caddy's hanger in place

prints.title: Lifting Claude
prints.description: A blocky Claude mascot holding a dumbbell in each hand, in orange, black, and dark gray PLA, rebuilt in OpenSCAD from an auto-traced original. This is the open-eye version; the squint-eyed variant and the original mesh are under Versions. The dumbbells slice at 1 h 42 min; the figure's time wasn't recorded.
prints.material: PLA, orange, black, and dark gray
prints.alt: A small blocky orange figure standing with a dark gray dumbbell in each hand and recessed black eyes

iterations.label: original mesh
iterations.note: The auto-traced original from 18 Feb 2026, with roughly 0.5 mm slants and asymmetries. Only the body is shown. Overall size is within about 0.2 mm of the later parametric rebuild.

photo.alt: Render of the auto-traced original Claude body, before the parametric rebuild

iterations.label: squint eyes
iterations.note: A variant with raised inward-pointing chevron eyes on a flat face, sharing the same body and dumbbells as the open-eye version. The open-eye design is the one shown as the main model.

photo.alt: Render of the squint-eyed Lifting Claude variant, with chevron eyes and dumbbells

prints.title: Robot vacuum
prints.description: Three prints used around a robot vacuum: a filter holder that sits in the dust bin under its hinged top door, a bumper that caps the end of a standing-desk T-foot so the vacuum can't climb it, and a bumper that fills the gap under a coffee table's base board, between its bun feet, so the vacuum can't wedge underneath.
prints.alt: A shallow two-bay filter tray, a long U-shaped desk-foot bumper, and a short bar bumper with two screw holes, all in charcoal

photos.alt: A black bumper capping the end of a T-shaped standing-desk foot, on beige carpet
Beige bumpers under the plinth of a dark wood coffee table, closing the gap above the rug
An open robovac dust bin held in a hand, with its hinged top door raised
The underside of a circular robot vacuum, showing the main brush, wheels, and a side brush

prints.title: Chicken coop
prints.description: A small model of a fenced chicken-coop yard with a green floor and a white picket fence, and a brown sign with black engraved lettering that reads "Chick Toys $3 ea." I didn't print the chickens; they're only shown for scale.
prints.material: PLA, green floor, white fence, brown sign with black lettering
prints.alt: A miniature square picket-fence yard with a green floor, a white fence, and a small brown sign with black lettering in front

photos.alt: The printed coop on a workbench: a green floor and a white picket fence, filled with small white toy chickens
photos.caption: I didn't print the chickens.

prints.title: Lid hanger
prints.description: A Tupperware lid hanger that mounts to the underside of a cabinet's top. Lids hang vertically from its row of downward slots.
prints.alt: A charcoal slotted lid hanger, a shallow rack with a row of downward slots

photos.alt: A tan lid hanger mounted to the underside of a white cabinet's top, with three clear lids hanging vertically from the slots

prints.title: Wedding rings
prints.description: A belt holster for a ring box: it clips onto a belt and carries the box on its side. It's shown with a 4 mm wedding band and the engagement ring, both in gold with the ring's three stones in pale blue, seated the way they sit in the slits of the box's cushion. The bands come in five widths, 3.0 to 5.0 mm in 0.5 mm steps; pick one under Band width, or see all five together.
prints.material: PLA Matte, charcoal holder; rings shown in gold
prints.alt: A boxy open-top belt holster with a gold wedding band and a gold engagement ring with pale blue stones floating inside it, lying flat one above the other where the ring box would hold them

variants.label: 3.0 mm
variants.note: A 3.0 mm wide band, inner diameter about 18.1 mm (about US size 8).

prints.title: Wild Things
prints.description: A pointed gold crown and a standing silver scepter with a gold ball in its cage.
prints.alt: A gold pointed crown and a tall silver scepter with a gold ball in its head, standing side by side

prints.title: Under-desk mounts
prints.description: Five mounts for the underside of my desk: a 200 mm and a 180 mm wire mount, a large and a small KVM mount, and a holder for the walking-pad remote. Show in setting lays them out the way they sit under the desk, with the desk upside-down so the view matches the photo.
prints.alt: A row of under-desk mounts: two square wire trays on corner legs, two T-shaped KVM mounts, and a small remote pocket

photos.alt: The underside of a wooden desk, with a metal frame rail, a walking-pad remote, cable and KVM gear, and power supplies
